descriptions.preferred: 'Beni shi en', which means "red smoke," is an unusual cultivar whose almost straplike deeply divided leaves change color all through the growing season. The foliage holds its colors well without burning, even in full sun in the southern United States. The young feathery leaves emerge a rosy red color, which changes to purple as the leaves develop, and then to medium green with a conspicuous light green midrib down each lobe. Many lobes develop an interesting light green edging, which sometimes broadens downward from the tips and may cause the lobes to become sickle shaped. The leaves take on a pinkish hue in late summer and slowly turn golden in the fall, the fall color lasting later than most cultivars. The five-lobed, sometimes seven-lobed, very deeply divided leaves are mostly longer than wide, 6-9 cm long and 5-7. 5 cm wide. The lobes are long, narrow oblongovate, coarsely toothed, 5-10 mm wide at the widest point in the middle, and with long tail-like tips. Each leaf is divided almost to the leaf base though, oddly, the distance between the lobe divisions to the petiole on the same leaf can vary between 5 and 20 mm. Most leaves fit the above description, but some leaves are much longer and coarser with broader lobes—8-12 cm long and 8-10 cm wide, with the lobes 1-1. 5 cm broad. Occasionally, some leaves are distorted. The slender green petioles are 2-3 cm long. This cultivar is moderately vigorous and forms a small upright tree. It requires full sun or partial shade and a reasonably well-drained soil. 'Beni shi en' was discovered and propagated by Harold Johnston of Tallassee, Alabama, from a witches'-broom on an Acer palma-

sources.name: Beni Shi En Red Japanese Maple
sources.description: This variegated grafted japanese maple is also known as “red smoke”. Leaf color changes all through the growing season. Spring is rosy red, then purple, then green, and finally pink in late summer. Fall colors are gold. Matures at 5 meters. Beni shi en is a rare maple if you are looking for something different.

descriptions_zh.preferred: ‘Beni shi en’意为“红烟”，是一个较为罕见的品种，其近乎带状、深裂的叶片在整个生长季都会持续变色。 其叶色保持性很好，即使在美国南部的全日照条件下也不易焦叶。 新生的羽状幼叶呈玫瑰红色，随后随着叶片发育转为紫色，再变为中绿色，每个裂片中央都有明显的浅绿色主脉。 许多裂片会形成颇具特色的浅绿色镶边，这种镶边有时会从裂片尖端向下扩展，并可能使裂片呈镰刀状。 夏末叶片会带有淡粉色调，秋季再缓慢转为金黄色，其秋色保持时间比多数品种更晚。 叶片通常为五裂，有时七裂，裂刻极深，多数长度大于宽度，长 6-9 厘米、宽 5-7. 5 厘米。 裂片狭长，呈长椭圆状卵形，边缘具粗齿，中部最宽处为 5-10 毫米，先端具长尾状尖。 每片叶几乎裂至叶基，但较为特殊的是，同一片叶上各裂片分裂处至叶柄的距离可在 5-20 毫米之间变化。 大多数叶片符合上述描述，但也有一些叶片明显更长、更粗犷，裂片更宽，长 8-12 厘米、宽 8-10 厘米，裂片宽 1-1. 5 厘米。 偶尔也会出现少量畸形叶。 细长的绿色叶柄长 2-3 厘米。 该品种长势中等，最终形成一株小型直立乔木。 栽培上需要全日照或半阴环境，以及排水较好的土壤。 ‘Beni shi en’由美国阿拉巴马州 Tallassee 的 Harold Johnston 从一株 Acer palma- 上的丛枝变异中发现并繁殖。
